A_target.statement:
Let $V$ be a [[Definition:Vector Space|vector space]] over a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]] $K$ and $\map {\Bbb P} V$ its [[Definition:Projective Space|projectivization]].
Then [[Definition:Mapping|mappings]] $f: \map {\Bbb P} V \to Z$ correspond to mappings $\tilde f: V \setminus \set {\mathbf 0} \to Z$ with:
:$\forall t \in K^\times: \map {\tilde f} {t \mathbf v} = \map {\tilde f} {\mathbf v}$

B_source.statement:
Let a [[Definition:Group|group]] $G$ [[Definition:Group Action|act]] on a set $X$.
Then mappings $X / G \to Z$ correspond to $G$-[[Definition:Invariant Mapping|invariant]] mappings $X \to Z$.

substitutions.the object acted upon: the set of nonzero vectors of the vector space

derived.invariant maps out of the object: maps on nonzero vectors constant on each line
derived.the induced map on the quotient: the corresponding map on projective space

validity_conditions: The scalar action on nonzero vectors is free, so its orbits are exactly the punctured lines through the origin.
A map is constant on orbits precisely when it is invariant under rescaling, which is the condition for descending to the quotient.
The origin must be removed for the action to be free; including it would collapse the whole space to a single extra orbit and destroy the correspondence.
proof_plan:
Remove the origin.
Then $K^\times$ acts [[Definition:Free Group Action|freely]] on $V \setminus \set {\mathbf 0}$ by scalar multiplication.

Form the [[Definition:Orbit Space|orbit space]]:
:$\map {\Bbb P} V = \paren {V \setminus \set {\mathbf 0} } / K^\times$
whose points are the lines through the origin.
By the source result, mappings out of the orbit space correspond to $K^\times$-invariant mappings, that is, rescaling-invariant mappings on $V \setminus \set {\mathbf 0}$.

Hence the stated classification of mappings out of projective space.
{{qed}}
